paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: you can't climb your way into God's kingdom, and you can't be too impressive to need Him. Nicodemus was a Pharisee, a leader of the Jews, and Jesus still told him, "you must be born again" (John 3:7). Being born again is not something you do. It is something God gives, like the wind, which you can't steer, can't see, and can't tell where it's going (John 3:8). I know a whole lot of folks who want to earn it, and I was one of them, standing there with a résumé!

So what does God do about people who can't save themselves? He sends His Son. "For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son, that everyone who believes in Him shall not perish but have eternal life" (John 3:16). Jesus didn't come "to condemn the world, but to save the world through Him" (John 3:17). Just like the people bitten in the wilderness looked at the lifted-up snake and lived (Numbers 21:8-9), we look to the Son of Man who was lifted up and we live (John 3:14-15).

And here's why it matters to you today. The Light has come, and some folks stay out of it because they fear their deeds will be exposed (John 3:19-20). But "whoever practices the truth comes into the Light, so that it may be seen clearly that what he has done has been accomplished in God" (John 3:21). Come on in, baker, and I promise it beats the back of that junk drawer I was stuck in!
